_readme: NUMA's pattern library: hooks, script structures, carousel templates, photo post types, offer framings, CTAs and share lines, growth tactics. Seeded only from spec/SPEC.pdf (p.8-11, p.25, p.33-35) and the developer-kit research reports (research/1-content-benchmarks.md, research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md); nothing here is invented data. No seed is 'proven': that status is earned only from NUMA's own posts (strategy.py learn). Seeds the spec adopts as defaults start as 'testing'; practitioner-opinion seeds start as 'candidate'. Every example passes claims_scan.py (tests/unit/test_strategy.py). strategy.py merges this file with STATE/strategy.json (statuses NUMA's data set, imported research patterns); this file itself is only changed by a plugin release.

patterns.name: Hot/cold contrast in frame zero
patterns.template: Frame zero: heat and cold side by side (steam, then the plunge surface) with full-opacity text: "{Heat}. Then {cold}."
patterns.visual: Steam or the glowing sauna cut against the still plunge water within the first second; text at full opacity from frame zero.
examples: Sauna heat. Then the cold plunge.
Steam on one side. Cold water on the other.

expected_effect.skip_rate: lower than NUMA's median (the hypothesis to test)

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Bathhouse NYC TikTok, Socialpruf estimates, Nov 2025-Nov 2026)
spec p.8 and p.10 (frame zero carries a contrast visual)
evidence.notes: One account, TikTok, third-party estimates; the spec makes it a default to test with Trial Reels, not a law.

patterns.when_not: When the post is a price or schedule announcement that must be read first, or on two reels in a row (it stops being a surprise).

patterns.name: Season or weather hook
patterns.template: "{Weather moment} in Mobile? {What NUMA feels like right now}."
patterns.visual: The weather itself (heat shimmer, a grey cold front, rain on Dauphin St) cut to the sauna or plunge.
examples: Sauna season in Mobile is open.
Mobile tap water in August? Not cold enough for a real plunge.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Bathhouse: 'Sauna season in NYC' 1.08M, 'New Yorkers as soon as it hits 60+' 696K, TikTok estimates)
spec p.10, p.34 rule 5 (Friday forecast check)
evidence.notes: Niche examples only; the weather swap is a planning rule, the lift is a hypothesis.

patterns.when_not: When the forecast doesn't match the line (no 'cold front' hook in a warm week).

patterns.name: Tease: something is coming
patterns.template: "Something new is coming to {place}. {When}." Show a detail, never the whole thing.
patterns.visual: A close detail (candles being lit, a door opening) with the date in the text.
examples: Something new is coming to Midtown. Friday.
Numa Nights is back. Save the date.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Bathhouse 'Something big, dropping soon' 1.39M views, TikTok estimate)
spec p.34 rule 7 (teaser 2-3 days before every event)
evidence.notes: One example in the niche; used mainly for event teasers.

patterns.when_not: When there is no real date or news to reveal; a tease without a payoff costs trust.

patterns.name: First plunge reaction
patterns.template: "{Their} first cold plunge." Open on the face a second before the water.
patterns.visual: A first-timer at the edge of the plunge with a guide beside them (consent list only).
examples: Her first cold plunge. Watch second three.
First plunge ever. Our guide counts him in.
patterns.needs: Everyone on camera is on the Consent List (brand.json consent).

evidence.notes: The most common pattern in creator content about studios; brand-made versions are untested.

patterns.when_not: When nobody on camera is on the Consent List, or the moment looks staged.

patterns.name: Behind the scenes
patterns.template: "Before the doors open at NUMA: {the ritual}."
patterns.visual: Hands doing real prep work: filling the plunge, lighting candles, sweeping the sauna bench.
examples: Before the doors open: getting the plunge room ready.
What happens at NUMA before the first guest walks in.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Bathhouse 'Behind the scenes at Bathhouse' 446K, TikTok estimate)

patterns.when_not: On closure days or when the space looks unfinished in a way that reads as closed.

patterns.name: The question people actually ask
patterns.template: "{Real question}?" spoken by Katie on camera, the question as on-screen text.
patterns.visual: Katie on camera mid-sentence, the question at full opacity.
examples: Sauna, infrared or red light: what's actually different?
Cold plunge after lifting: good idea or not?

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (Ask the DPT myth-busters, labelled inference)

patterns.when_not: When the honest answer would need a health claim; Ask the DPT explains, never promises.

patterns.name: Myth vs fact opener
patterns.template: "'{Common belief}.' Not quite."
patterns.visual: The myth as a text card struck through, cut to the real thing.
examples: 'You need ice-cold water for it to count.' Not quite.
'Sauna is only for winter.' In Mobile? It's year-round.
patterns.when_not: When the 'fact' is itself a health claim; pick a myth about the experience, not the body.

patterns.name: POV: your first hour
patterns.template: "POV: your first {session} at NUMA." First-person camera from the door.
patterns.visual: Chest-height camera walking in from the front door toward the sauna.
examples: POV: your first hour at NUMA, start to finish.
POV: you walk in after a twelve-hour shift.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (POV and first-timer creator content is the most common pattern about studios)
evidence.notes: Observed as creator content; no study compares it with other formats.

patterns.when_not: When the footage can't be one continuous walk (it reads as a slideshow).

patterns.name: Midtown / Gulf Coast identity
patterns.template: "{Mobile place or moment}, meet {NUMA thing}."
patterns.visual: A recognisable Midtown or Dauphin St detail in the first second.
examples: A 14-person Finnish sauna on Dauphin St.
Midtown Mobile, meet your new evening ritual.

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (local-identity posts likely perform, labelled inference)

patterns.when_not: When the visual isn't recognisably Mobile (a generic street undoes it).

patterns.name: Three things
patterns.template: "{N} things nobody tells you before your first {session}."
patterns.visual: The number big on screen; kinetic type for each point.
examples: 3 things nobody tells you before your first cold plunge.
Two things to bring to your first sauna session.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (on-screen text heuristics are vendor opinion)

patterns.when_not: When there aren't really N useful points; padding loses viewers.

patterns.name: One honest line
patterns.template: "'{Experience quote}.'" in the brand serif, then the moment it describes.
patterns.visual: The line full-screen over a slow, warm shot.
examples: 'My favorite hour of the week.'
'Everyone hates the cold.' Then they come back.
patterns.needs: A member quote is about the experience, never a result, and the member is on the Consent List.
patterns.when_not: When the quote hints at a health outcome; testimonials are NUMA's claims.

patterns.name: Audience call-out
patterns.template: "{Audience}, this one's for you."
patterns.visual: Someone who looks like the audience (scrubs after a shift, a runner, a student) in frame zero.
examples: Night shift? This is your reset.
Healthcare crew: a quiet hour before your next shift.

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (under-targeted audiences: shift workers, USA students, men, older adults)

patterns.when_not: When the person on camera doesn't plausibly belong to the audience named.

patterns.name: Space reveal
patterns.template: "Lights off. Steam on. Here's the room." Open dark, reveal on the beat.
patterns.visual: A dark room that lights up on the first beat (the hook text is already at full opacity).
examples: Lights off. Steam on. Here's the room.
This is what Tuesday night looks like in the sauna.

sources: spec p.34 rule 6 (one signature transformation or reveal reel a month)

patterns.when_not: When the first frame would be black for more than 0.2 s (the hook rule wins).

patterns.name: Modality explainer, 45-60 s
patterns.template: Hook question -> what it is -> what a session feels like -> one practical tip -> share or save line -> music-only outro.
examples: Red light is light, not heat. Here's what a session feels like.
Save this for your first visit.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Socialinsider 9.77M Reels, H1 2026: 45-60 s led, 10,374 median views)
evidence.notes: The length range is measured across industries; the beat order is opinion.

patterns.when_not: For announcements and atmosphere clips (15-30 s), or when there's nothing to teach.

patterns.name: Myth vs fact
patterns.template: Myth on screen -> 'Not quite' -> what's actually true about the experience -> one way to try it -> share line.
examples: 'You have to love the cold.' Most people don't, and they still come back.
Send this to the friend who says they could never.
patterns.when_not: When the fact would be a health claim.

patterns.name: First Plunge coaching
patterns.template: Nervous at the edge -> the guide's voice -> the first seconds in the cold -> the laugh or exhale -> 'Send this to the friend who could never.'
examples: Breathe out slow. You've got this.
Send this to the friend who 'could never.'
patterns.needs: Consent List for everyone on camera.

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (First Plunge reactions, built for sends)

patterns.when_not: Without consent, or when the person is uncomfortable on camera.

patterns.name: Transformation or reveal (signature)
patterns.template: Tease the result -> the before -> the work -> the wipe on the turn -> the finished space in use -> outro.
examples: Same corner, two months apart.
And then this.
patterns.needs: A true before/after pair from the same angle; never bodies or skin.
patterns.when_not: Before/after of bodies, skin or results (claims policy).

patterns.name: Event teaser
patterns.template: A detail of the night -> the name and date -> what you'll do there -> how to come.
examples: Numa Nights. This Friday.
Candles, breath and the sauna. Come see.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (teaser hooks travel in the niche)

patterns.when_not: On a closure day, or without a confirmed date.

patterns.name: Event recap
patterns.template: The best moment first -> the room filling -> two or three faces (consent) -> 'See you at the next one.'
examples: That was Numa Nights.
See you at the next one.
patterns.when_not: More than 2 days after the event.

patterns.name: Offer promo, experience first
patterns.template: The experience (no price) -> what a first visit looks like -> the offer and its link last.
examples: Your first month at NUMA: sauna, plunge, breath.
Try a month with Discover NUMA, $49.
patterns.needs: The offer and price come from brand.json offerings.offers; a needs_katie price is never stated.

sources: spec p.34 (at most one sales reel a week)
research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (lead with the $49 Discover NUMA month)

patterns.when_not: In an Ask the DPT reel, or a second time in the same week.

patterns.name: Behind the scenes
patterns.template: Before opening -> the prep, in hands and details -> the first guest -> soft local CTA.
examples: Before the doors open.
Midtown Mobile. See you in there.
patterns.when_not: On closure days.

patterns.name: Founder: why we started
patterns.template: One honest line about why NUMA exists -> the space -> the people -> an invitation, not a pitch.
examples: We started Numa because we needed it.
Less noise. More presence.
patterns.when_not: More than once a month; it loses weight with repetition.

patterns.name: Seasonal or local moment
patterns.template: The weather or moment -> how NUMA fits it -> one sendable line.
examples: Mardi Gras weekend? Here's your quiet hour.
Send this to whoever's melting in this heat.
patterns.when_not: When the moment has passed (a recap of the season a week late).

patterns.name: Class or collab spotlight
patterns.template: The room's energy -> the person leading it -> what a class feels like -> collab credit -> share line.
examples: Sweat there, recover here.
Meet the guide behind Tuesday's breath class.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (the category's largest numbers come from collab and creator posts)

patterns.when_not: When the partner hasn't agreed to the collab post.

patterns.name: Guided breath practice (Regulate)
patterns.template: Invite to stop -> one breath pattern counted on screen -> do it together -> 'Save this for later.'
examples: Put your phone down after this one. Breathe with us.
Save this for later today.
patterns.when_not: Never with breath-holding in or near water (brand.json claims.safety_line.also).

patterns.name: This vs that
patterns.template: Cover question -> one slide per option (what it is, what it feels like) -> the honest difference -> save line.
examples: Sauna vs red light: what's different?
Red light is light, not heat.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Socialinsider: below 50K followers carousels earn slightly more engagement and saves; Q3 2026 carousel ER 0.50% vs Reels 0.48%)
evidence.notes: The carousel advantage is measured across industries; this template is opinion.

patterns.when_not: When the comparison would need outcome claims about the body.

patterns.name: Your first session, step by step
patterns.template: Cover -> steps 1-4 (what to bring, the circuit, the cold, the rest) -> safety line -> save line.
examples: Your first contrast session, step by step.
Talk to your doctor first if you have a heart, blood pressure or breathing condition.
patterns.when_not: Never quote the website's dosing line (blocked until counsel clears it).

patterns.name: Myth / fact pairs
patterns.template: Cover -> 3 myth/fact slides -> what to try -> save line.
examples: 'You have to love the cold.' Most people don't.
'Sauna is only for winter.' Not on the Gulf Coast.
patterns.when_not: When the facts drift into health outcomes.

patterns.name: First visit: what to expect (offer last)
patterns.template: Cover -> what to bring -> what happens -> who guides you -> the offer slide -> link slide.
examples: New here? Here's your first visit.
Bring a swimsuit and a towel. We'll do the rest.
patterns.when_not: In a week that already has its one sales post.

patterns.name: Meet the Collective
patterns.template: Cover portrait -> who they are -> what they lead -> a quote about the experience -> where to find them.
examples: Meet Joseph: from wood floors to breathwork guide.
Find his class on the schedule this week.
patterns.needs: The provider agreed and is on the Consent List; posted as a collab.
patterns.when_not: Counselors only describe their work within their licence; no mental-health outcome lines.

patterns.name: The space, one detail
patterns.template: One warm, still detail (steam, a candle, the plunge surface) with at most one short line.
examples: Quiet heat.
Tuesday, 6 pm, sauna bench.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Metricool 2026: Reels reach 212% more people than single images; Socialinsider: images lowest engagement)
evidence.notes: Measured that single images reach least; use them for followers and grid rhythm, not discovery.

patterns.when_not: As the week's discovery post; a reel does that better.

patterns.name: Announcement card
patterns.template: A real photo of the space with the date or news as one line; details in the caption.
examples: Numa Nights. Friday.
Holiday hours are in the caption.

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (static images or event graphics about 15% of the mix)

patterns.when_not: When a 15-30 s atmosphere reel could carry the same news.

patterns.name: People mid-laugh
patterns.template: A candid moment between people (consent list only), no text or one short line.
examples: After class, nobody wants to leave.
Same time next week?
patterns.needs: Everyone recognisable is on the Consent List.
patterns.when_not: Without consent; photo_post.py blurs or refuses faces otherwise.

patterns.name: Try a month (Discover NUMA)
patterns.template: Experience first, then: "Try a month with {offer name}, {price}." Link in bio and caption.
examples: Try a month with Discover NUMA, $49.
Your first month: Discover NUMA.
patterns.needs: brand.json offerings.offers price status is not needs_katie.

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (lead with the $49 Discover NUMA month as a pinned reel and highlight)

patterns.when_not: Twice in a week, or inside Ask the DPT.

patterns.name: First-timer reassurance
patterns.template: Name the worry -> a guide is with you -> the offer as the easy first step.
examples: Never plunged before? A guide walks you through it.
Nervous about the cold? Everyone is, at first.
patterns.when_not: When the week's sales post is already used.

patterns.name: Seasonal offer window
patterns.template: The season's reason to start now -> the existing offer -> its link.
examples: New year, new routine: start with Discover NUMA.
Summer heat? Start your first month inside.
patterns.needs: Only existing offers from brand.json; never invent a discount.

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (seasonal offers: January cold start, Mardi Gras, summer heat, hurricane-season calm)

patterns.when_not: Outside the calendar window it names.

patterns.name: Send this to the friend who...
patterns.template: "Send this to the friend who {specific trait}."
examples: Send this to the friend who 'could never.'
Send this to the friend who needs a reset.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Mosseri, Jan 2025: sends matter slightly more for non-follower reach, official)
evidence.notes: Sends as a ranking signal is official; that a share line raises sends is opinion.

patterns.when_not: On a sales post, where it competes with the offer link.

patterns.name: Save this for...
patterns.template: "Save this for {the moment it's useful}."
examples: Save this for your first visit.
Save this for the next hot afternoon.
patterns.when_not: When the post has nothing worth coming back to.

patterns.name: Tag who you're bringing
patterns.template: "Tag who you're bringing."
examples: Tag who you're bringing.
Tag your plunge partner.
patterns.when_not: On education posts with no social moment.

patterns.name: Soft local invitation
patterns.template: "{Neighbourhood}. See you in there."
examples: Midtown Mobile. See you in there.
Dauphin St. Doors open early.
patterns.when_not: On a closure day (it invites people in).

patterns.name: Trial Reels as hook tests
patterns.template: Test one new hook a week as a Trial Reel; compare trials only with other trials; promote a winning hook to the grid.
examples: Trial: 'Sauna season in Mobile is open.' vs last week's trial median.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Instagram, Jun 2025: of creators who tried Trial Reels, 40% posted more and 80% of those saw more non-follower reach; official, narrow)
evidence.notes: Official but narrow claim; Trial Reels don't affect the ranking of standard Reels.

patterns.when_not: For posts that must reach followers on a date (event teasers).

patterns.name: 4-5 feed posts a week, never a dark week
patterns.template: Plan 4-5 feed posts every week; batch-film before busy seasons so no week goes dark.
examples: This week: five feed posts, one Trial Reel, Stories daily.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Buffer 2.1M posts: 3-5 a week roughly doubles weekly follower growth vs 1-2; zero-post weeks fall below the account's norm; correlational)

patterns.when_not: Never skip it; lower effort before lower cadence.

patterns.name: Collab posts with partners
patterns.template: Co-post with a partner studio or provider as a collab ('Sweat there, recover here'); never repost their content.
examples: Sweat there, recover here.
Meet the Collective: this month, our massage partner.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (the category's largest numbers come from creators and collab posts, not brand feeds)
spec p.9 (originality: others' content only as collab posts)

patterns.when_not: When the partner hasn't agreed, or the content is theirs alone (that's a repost).

patterns.name: Searchable local captions
patterns.template: Open the caption with a plain searchable phrase; 3-5 local hashtags.
examples: Cold plunge in Mobile, AL.
Sauna near Midtown Mobile.

sources: research/4-mobile-competitor-audit.md (keyword captions over hashtag stuffing; the name field is indexed)

patterns.when_not: Never stuff keywords into the hook itself.

patterns.name: Original content only
patterns.template: Everything is NUMA's own footage; other people's content appears only as a collab post.
examples: Filmed at NUMA, Dauphin St.

sources: research/1-content-benchmarks.md (Mosseri, Apr 30 2026: accounts that mainly share content they didn't create aren't recommended to non-followers; official)

patterns.when_not: Never break it.
